messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: high-severity - egress 5xx spike detected in euc1-azf (ALB -> Envoy -> upstream). Synthetic checks + edge metrics triggered. Runbook: https://redwood.ops/runbooks/egress-5xx -- paging on-call SRE.

sre-oncall: I'm on it, taking incident commander. @network-eng can you start with routing + DNS checks? I'll triage customer impact and coordinate mitigations.

network-eng: looking. early signals show a sharp increase in connection resets from euc1-azf to our upstream transit provider (AS64512). Route53 RTTs to euc1 edge are normal but traffic to some next-hop IPs is being blackholed by provider. Could be a path flap.

alice: from edge dashboards: ALB target group "egress-tg-azf" 5xx rate jumped from 0.6% -> 18% in 2m. Top errors are 502/504 + TLS handshake errors. Sample curl from edge to one upstream IP: ``curl -v https://10.12.34.56/health`` -> connection reset by peer.

matt: envoy logs from ingress-proxy (euc1-azf) show repeated ``connection reset before response completed`` and ``upstream connect error or disconnect``. Paste of log snippet:

```
[2026-03-15T21:02:11Z] envoy upstream error: connection reset, upstream:10.12.34.56:443, downstream:10.0.5.12:51982
[2026-03-15T21:02:13Z] envoy healthcheck failure: tcp_connect_timeout
```

dena: likely root cause = upstream provider path misroute or overloaded NAT. Short mitigation options:
- remove AZ targets from ALB target group (drain) to stop forwarding traffic to bad path
- shift Route53 weighted traffic from euc1 -> euc2 for affected records
- restart ingress-controller pods in euc1-azf (quick to reclaim connections)
I recommend doing weighted DNS shift first to reduce blast radius, then drain targets.

ops-rotation: making a Route53 change now: increasing euc2 weight from 30 -> 80 for service records behind *.api.euc1.redwood.com. ChangeID: ZDOGE-9876. TTL respected, expect ~60s propagation for commit, but clients may cache.

sre-oncall: executing ALB mitigation: setting target group "egress-tg-azf" to draining and reducing deregistration delay to 5s. Command used:
```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:aws:...:egress-tg-azf --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=5
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:...:egress-tg-azf --targets Id=i-0abc123
```

deploy-bot: restarted 3 ingress-controller pods in euc1-azf (kube-system/ingress-controller) via rolling restart. ```kubectl rollout restart deployment/ingress-controller -n kube-system --context euc1-azf```

alice: immediate metric check: edge 5xxs reduced from 18% -> 9% after DNS shift + drain. Latency for successful requests is stable. Still seeing connection resets to two upstream IPs (10.12.34.56, 10.12.34.57).

eng-prod: can we confirm which customers hit the egress path? I can pull request logs.

sre-oncall: initial customer impact: approximately 19% of requests for tenant-42 and ~12% for tenant-114 failed during the peak window. Total requests affected ~14k in 15m window. No data exfiltration indicators. Email/CS update recommended.

customer-success: copying CS. We'll draft advisory: "Service degradation in euc1 region for some customers, mitigations in progress, ETA for full remediation TBD." Tag me for review.

network-eng: I'm engaging transit provider NOC now (ticket #TN-22071). They've confirmed flapping on a specific peer and are investigating upstream route suppression for the /24. Meanwhile we should keep euc2 weight high and avoid reintroducing targets in azf.

dena: action items captured:
- keep Route53 weights moved to euc2 until provider confirms fix (ops-rotation)
- keep egress-tg-azf drained (sre-oncall)
- postmortem owner: @eng-prod (assign after incident)
- escalate change to infra leadership if provider fix > 2 hours

ops-rotation: provider NOC responded: their team sees intermittent blackholes on peer 203.0.113.45 -> they've rerouted for mitigation, monitoring now. They expect stabilization within 20-40 minutes.

alice: monitoring update: 5xxs now ~4%, continuing downward trend. Removing euc1 targets would drop capacity but is safer.

matt: one note: ingress-controller restarts cleared many tcp connections; Envoy active connection counts down from ~48k -> ~12k across pods in azf.

sre-oncall: preparing incident summary for Slack and postmortem. Handing off to @dena for the next 4-hour watch. I'll update severity/until resolved. Thanks everyone.

dena: taking handoff. I'll keep the channel updated, continue checks on provider ticket TN-22071, and coordinate with CS for customer comms. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident status changed: mitigated -> monitoring. Participants: sre-oncall, dena, network-eng, ops-rotation. Next update due in 30m.
